back: A junction between two neurones (or a neurone and an effector) across which information passes by a chemical neurotransmitter.

front: First events when an action potential reaches a presynaptic knob
back: Voltage-gated Ca²⁺ channels open; Ca²⁺ diffuses in; vesicles fuse with the membrane and release ACh by exocytosis.

front: What happens when ACh binds to postsynaptic receptors?
back: Receptor Na⁺ channels open; Na⁺ diffuses in and depolarises the postsynaptic membrane; action potential if threshold is reached.
Choline and ethanoic acid (acetate); recycled into the presynaptic knob.
Temporal: repeated impulses from one neurone add up. Spatial: impulses from several neurones arriving together add up.

front: Why is transmission at a synapse one-way?
back: Vesicles of transmitter are only in the presynaptic knob; receptors only on the postsynaptic membrane.
Inhibit acetylcholinesterase, so ACh is not broken down and postsynaptic cells are continuously stimulated.

front: How does nicotine act at synapses?
back: Similar shape to ACh; binds some ACh receptors and opens their channels (mimics ACh).
One-way transmission, summation (filtering weak signals), integration of many inputs, divergence and convergence.
